frs_sections.title: The Display Serial Interface Specification defines protocols between a host processor and peripheral
frs_sections.content:
231   devices that adhere to MIPI Alliance specifications for mobile device interfaces. The DSI specification
232   builds on existing specifications by adopting pixel formats and command set defined in MIPI Alliance
233   specifications for DBI-2[2], DPI-2[3], and DCS[1].


234   1.1    Scope

frs_sections.title: Interface protocols as well as a description of signal timing relationships are within the scope of this
frs_sections.content:
236   document.

237   Electrical specifications and physical specifications are out of scope for this document. In addition, legacy
238   interfaces such as DPI-2 and DBI-2 are also out of scope for this document. Furthermore, device usage of
239   auxiliary buses such as I2C or SPI, while not precluded by this specification, are also not within its scope.


240   1.2    Purpose

frs_sections.title: The Display Serial Interface specification defines a high-speed serial interface between a peripheral, such
frs_sections.content:
242   as an active-matrix display module, and a host processor in a mobile device. By standardizing this
243   interface, components may be developed that provide higher performance, lower power, less EMI and
244   fewer pins than current devices, while maintaining compatibility across products from multiple vendors.

protocol_overview.type: Packet-based half-duplex bidirectional serial display interface on top of source-synchronous DDR D-PHY physical layer; combines DPI-2 pixel streaming (Video Mode) and DBI-2-style command/parameter transport (Command Mode) into one serialized link.
protocol_overview.duplex: Half-duplex per Data Lane 0 (the only bidirectional lane); additional Data Lanes 1..3 are strictly unidirectional host → peripheral.
wire_names: Data0+ / Data0- (Data Lane 0 — bidirectional in LP)
protocol_overview.dual_mode_signaling: HS (high-speed differential 100-200 mV terminated) + LP (low-power 1.2 V single-ended) on the same Dp/Dn pair; mode arbitrated by the lane-state controller.
protocol_overview.DDR_clock: Source-synchronous DDR Clock Lane — both edges latch one bit per Data Lane; data-rate-per-lane = 2 × Clock-Lane Hz. Clock Lane is host → peripheral only (never reversed).
protocol_overview.controller_role: Host processor: drives Clock Lane; transmits all forward-direction HS / LP packets; initiates BTA; programs T_INIT_MASTER ≥ t_POR + T_INIT_SLAVE + T_INTERNAL_DELAY at power-up.
protocol_overview.target_role: Peripheral (display module): receives forward HS / LP packets; after BTA, transmits LP reverse-direction packets (Acknowledge, Acknowledge and Error Report, Read Response, Tearing Effect trigger message); returns bus to host with its own BTA.

compliance_requirements: Sync pattern, HS Entry / Exit, lane-state encoding inherit from MIPI D-PHY v0.90.00.
Packet Header ECC = Hamming-modified single-bit-correct / 2-bit-detect over 24-bit DI + WC.
Long-Packet Payload Checksum = 16-bit CRC, polynomial x^16+x^12+x^5+1, init 0xFFFF, LSB-first.
All DSI transmitters and receivers shall support Continuous Clock behavior on the Clock Lane.
Host LP clock frequency shall be in the range 67%..150% of peripheral LP clock frequency.
Set Maximum Return Packet Size (0x37) default value at power-on or reset shall be 1.
Reserved bit positions in the Error Report (bits 7 and 14) shall be sent as 0.

functional_requirements.text: DSI peripherals shall support either Command Mode (DCS commands + frame buffer at peripheral) or Video Mode (real-time pixel streaming from host), or both.
Host shall implement at minimum 1 Data Lane plus 1 Clock Lane; additional Data Lanes 1..3 are optional.
Clock Lane shall be driven by the host processor only, never by the peripheral. Continuous Clock Mode shall be supported by all DSI transmitters and receivers.
In a Command Mode system, Data Lane 0 shall be bidirectional; additional Data Lanes shall be unidirectional. In a Video Mode system, Data Lane 0 may be bidirectional or unidirectional.
Forward-direction Low Power transmissions shall use Data Lane 0 only. Reverse-direction transmissions shall use Low Power Mode only and shall use Data Lane 0 only.
DSI shall transport data using Short Packet (4 bytes) and Long Packet (6..65541 bytes) per §8.4.
Data Identifier byte DI[7:0] = VC[7:6] (Virtual Channel, 4 channels) + DT[5:0] (Data Type).

Every Packet Header shall carry an 8-bit ECC providing single-bit error correction + 2-bit error detection over DI + WC using a Hamming-modified code. P6 and P7 are unused and shall be 0 by transmitter; receiver shall ignore P6/P7 and force them to 0 before processing.
Long Packet Payload Checksum shall be 16-bit CRC poly x^16+x^12+x^5+1, init 0xFFFF, LSB-first, covering payload only. Zero-length payload Checksum = 0xFFFF. Non-checksum peripheral Checksum = 0x0000.
All packet data traverses LSB-first within each byte; multi-byte fields LS byte first unless otherwise specified.

Devices compliant with DSI v1.01 shall support EoTp Short Packet (DT = 0x08, VC = 0, payload = 0x0F0F, ECC = 0x01). EoTp shall be sent at end of every HS transmission when enabled, NOT for LP transmissions. Devices shall provide a means to enable / disable EoTp.
Bus Turn-Around shall use D-PHY LP Escape Mode mechanism. Host asserts TurnRequest; peripheral responds; peripheral hands bus back via own TurnRequest.
Peripheral shall respond with one or more appropriate packets after every host transmission that asserts BTA, then return bus ownership.
Up to four Virtual Channels (VC[1:0]) shall be supported.
Peripheral shall implement ECC checking; Checksum checking is optional. Errors reported via Acknowledge and Error Report Short Packet (DT = 0x02) after BTA.
Bidirectional peripheral shall implement HRX_TO and LTX-P_TO. Host shall implement HTX_TO and LRX-H_TO. LRX-H_TO must be set longer than LTX-P_TO.
Host shall drive sustained LP-11 TX-Stop for T_INIT at power-up. Host's T_INIT_MASTER ≥ t_POR + T_INIT_SLAVE + T_INTERNAL_DELAY of peripheral.
When N_data_lanes > 1, Lane Distributor sends bytes round-robin (byte k → lane (k mod N)); all Lanes start SoT in parallel; single common Clock Lane shared by all Data Lanes.
Tearing Effect from a Command Mode display module shall be transmitted as LP Escape trigger byte 0x5D (LSB-first 10111010); host first gives bus possession to peripheral via BTA without command.
Video Mode peripherals shall support at least one of three packet sequences: Non-Burst with Sync Pulses, Non-Burst with Sync Events, Burst Mode.
Command Mode peripherals shall support DCS (0x05 / 0x15 / 0x06 / 0x39 + 0x21 / 0x22 / 0x1C) on top of DSI Short/Long Packets.
Video Mode host SHALL implement all four pixel formats (RGB565 / RGB666 Packed / RGB666 Loosely Packed / RGB888). Peripheral SHALL implement at least one.
Maximum Return Packet Size defaults to 1 at power-on / reset. Host programs via Set Maximum Return Packet Size Short Packet (DT=0x37).
Data Type codes with DT[3:0] = 0b0000 or 0b1111 SHALL NOT be used. Other unspecified codes are Reserved.

configurations.name: Command Mode + 2..4 Lanes
configurations.description: Data Lane 0 bidirectional + 1..3 additional unidirectional Data Lanes.

configurations.name: Video Mode + 1..4 Lanes, unidirectional
configurations.description: Cost-optimized Video Mode display without on-panel buffer.

configurations.name: Video Mode + 1..4 Lanes, bidirectional
configurations.description: Video Mode with bidirectional Data Lane 0 for Acknowledge and Error Report.

configurations.name: Continuous Clock Mode
configurations.description: Clock Lane stays in HS forever; lowest latency.

configurations.name: Non-Continuous Clock Mode
configurations.description: Clock Lane returns to LP-11 between HS bursts; saves clock-tree power.

configurations.name: EoTp enabled
configurations.description: Every HS transmission ends with EoTp Short Packet (DT=0x08, payload 0x0F0F).

error_response_conditions: ECC single-bit error — corrected; Error Report bit 8 set.
ECC multi-bit error — packet dropped; bit 9 set; rest of transmission lost.
Checksum mismatch on Long Packet payload — bit 10 set.
DSI Protocol Violation — bit 15 set (expected EoTp / BTA not received).
SoT Error — bit 0 set; SoT Sync Error — bit 1; EoT Sync Error — bit 2.
Escape Mode Entry Command Error — bit 3; LP Transmit Sync Error — bit 4.
HS Receive Timeout Error — bit 5 set (HRX_TO expired).
LP Contention — Annex A recovery flow.
